name: Question 9
problem: The rate at which a liquid cools is proportional to the difference between its temperature and the temperature of its surroundings. Let $T(t)$ be the temperature of the liquid in degrees Celsius, and let $t>0$ be the time in minutes. If the temperature of the surroundings is ${25}^{∘}\text{C},$ which differential equation could be used to model the temperature of the liquid? Assume that $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality.

Question 9
?

The rate at which a liquid cools is proportional to the difference between its temperature and the temperature of its surroundings. Let T(t) be the temperature of the liquid in degrees Celsius, and let t>0 be the time in minutes. If the temperature of the surroundings is 25∘C, which differential equation could be used to model the temperature of the liquid? Assume that k>0 is a constant of proportionality.

a
T′(t)=−k(T−25)
b
T′(t)=k(T−25)
c
T′(t)=kT(T+25)
d
T′(t)=kT(T−25)
e
T′(t)=−kT(T−25)
